title: Large-scale iontronic skins with neural-hierarchical processing architecture - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
AbstractThe human skin gathers and encodes signals from over 200,000 mechanoreceptors, enabling high-spatiotemporal-resolution tactile perception and instant injury prevention. Existing skin-like sensor arrays often have limited sensor count and density, and they use a serial readout architecture that suffers from readout latency, signal crosstalk and bandwidth consumption as element density increases. Here we report a high-density (1,110 units cm‒2) and large-scale (>10,000 units) neural-hierarchical iontronic skin that mimics the hierarchical processing architecture of the human sensory system, which transmits interactive information in layers via signal encoding, convergence and cognitive modelling. Frequency-based position encoding of iontronic sensors enables parallel signal transmission with suppressed crosstalk and a rate of 100 frames per second, while backend convergent compression decreases bandwidth consumption by hundreds of times. We demonstrate that humanoid robots equipped with neural-hierarchical iontronic skins can perform challenging tasks, including fine tactile interactions that can resolve surface features of 300 µm, and the perception of nociceptive stimuli for self-protective responses. This technology provides a large-scale tactile system with high spatiotemporal resolution, paving the way for humanoid robots to approach human-level perception and manipulation.

Data availability

All data required to support the conclusions of this study are provided within the Article and its Supplementary Information. In addition, the tactile interaction datasets generated in this study are publicly available via GitHub at https://github.com/jioy/NI-skins.git (ref. 52).
Code availability

The codes that support the sensor data visualization, model training and interactive control are available via GitHub at https://github.com/jioy/NI-skins.git (ref. 52).
